data.title: Carvana Expands Same-Day Delivery to Southern New Hampshire
data.description:
Carvana (), the leading e-commerce platform for buying and selling cars, today announced the expansion of same-day delivery to eligible customers in southern New Hampshire. Customers can now buy a car entirely online at Carvana.com and have it delivered as soon as the same day. Local customers selling a vehicle to Carvana can also schedule pickup or drop-off as soon as the same day they complete the company’s online appraisal process.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261119129494/en/

Carvana expands same-day delivery to southern New Hampshire.

Same-day delivery service is now available in many cities across southern New Hampshire, including Manchester, Concord, Nashua, Portsmouth, Dover, and Rochester.

“My old car had stopped working, and I needed a replacement quickly,” said Joneil V., a southern New Hampshire customer. “I wasn’t sure what to expect when I went on Carvana.com, but buying the car was super easy and straightforward, and I could have it delivered that afternoon! Within 10 minutes of placing my order, I got a call with an exact arrival time and a rundown of the documents I’d need. They even kept me updated on traffic along the way. Being able to get my car that same day made the experience even better.”

Carvana’s intuitive e-commerce platform allows customers to shop from tens of thousands of high-quality vehicles, secure financing, trade in a vehicle, and complete a purchase entirely online. This offering is made possible with the support of Carvana’s first-party logistics network and regional Inspection and Reconditioning Centers (IRCs).

“We’re excited to bring same-day delivery to southern New Hampshire, offering local customers an even faster and more convenient way to buy or sell a car,” said Jacqueline Hearns, Carvana’s Senior Director of Market Operations and Expansion. “Our growing network and simple, technology-driven process make it possible for eligible customers to go from finding the right car online to having it in their driveway that same day.”

Initially launched in Arizona, Carvana’s same-day delivery service is currently available in select markets across more than 25 states. The company plans to continue scaling the offering regionally as it expands its national logistics and reconditioning infrastructure.

About Carvana

Carvana’s mission is to change the way people buy and sell cars. Since launching in 2013, more than 4 million customers have chosen Carvana’s leading automotive e-commerce experience to shop, sell, finance, and trade in vehicles entirely online, with the convenience of delivery or local pickup as soon as the same day. Carvana’s unique offering is powered by its passionate team, differentiated national infrastructure, and purpose-built technology.

For more information, please visit Carvana.com.

data.title: CareView Communications Announces New Business Agreement with DCH Health System
data.description:
CareView Communications, Inc. (“CareView” or the “Company”) (OTCQB: CRVW), a leader in virtual patient observation and AI-powered safety solutions, today announced a new business agreement with DCH Health System, a community-owned healthcare system based in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. DCH Health System operates several hospitals, as well as several specialty clinics.

The agreement represents another step in CareView’s continued expansion, bringing its patient safety technology to healthcare organizations focused on improving patient care and supporting clinical teams.

DCH Health System has served the healthcare needs of West Alabama for more than a century. The DCH Health System includes DCH Regional Medical Center, Northport Medical Center, and Fayette Medical Center, providing a broad range of healthcare services to communities throughout the region.

Through this new agreement, CareView will bring its Patient Safety System to DCH Health System, providing technology designed to support virtual observation and help clinical teams monitor patients at risk for falls or other safety-related events.

CareView’s Patient Safety System incorporates motion detection and real-time, two-way audio and video communication to help caregivers observe patients remotely and respond when intervention may be needed. The technology is designed to complement existing clinical workflows, support timely interventions, and help hospitals evaluate patient observation practices while managing the demands placed on nursing resources.

“Expanding our reach to organizations like DCH Health System reinforces CareView’s commitment to helping hospitals address patient safety challenges through technology,” said Sandra McRee, Chief Operating Officer of CareView. “We recognize the importance of equipping clinical teams with tools that support patient observation, enable timely communication, and help healthcare organizations pursue measurable improvements in care delivery. We look forward to supporting DCH Health System as we continue expanding our impact across the healthcare industry.”

The agreement aligns with CareView’s broader growth strategy of partnering with healthcare organizations seeking practical, technology-enabled approaches to patient safety and operational efficiency. As hospitals navigate staffing pressures, rising operational demands, and the need to deliver consistent, high-quality care, virtual observation solutions can provide additional support for clinical teams while helping organizations assess opportunities to improve utilization and resource allocation.

The agreement with DCH Health System marks another milestone in CareView’s ongoing efforts to expand its customer base and bring its patient safety technology to more healthcare providers.

About CareView Communications, Inc.

For more than a decade, CareView has empowered over 200 hospitals nationwide with its virtual nursing and virtual sitter solutions. The Company’s patient safety platform, supported by AI-enabled predictive tools, significantly reduces falls and alleviates staffing pressure – helping hospitals deliver more safe and efficient care. More information about the Company and its products and services are available at the Company’s website at https://www.care-view.com and https://www.linkedin.com/company/careview-communications/.

data.title: Canadian telecom M&A risks a costly encore
data.description:
By Pranav Kiran

Canadian dealmakers are dialing another wrong number. Telecommunications conglomerate Quebecor wants to buy larger rival Telus in a deal valued at C$60.6 billion ($42.35 billion), including net debt. The target has already rebuffed the offer and the deal math leaves little room for error. Shareholders should send this proposal to voicemail.

Including C$160 million in estimated operating cost savings, Telus would generate a little over C$4 billion in net operating profit after tax for the 2027 financial year, based on Visible Alpha data. That amounts to a return on investment of just 6.7%, coming in below Telus’ 7.6% weighted average cost of capital, according to Morningstar.

Fundamentally, Quebecor is asking Telus to buy into a familiar telecom mega-deal fantasy. Roughly two-thirds of the offer is in stock, meaning investors would have to trust that the combined company can speedily cut down an enlarged debt pile. Quebecor thinks slashing stock buybacks and capital expenditures will lower leverage to 3.5 times EBITDA from 4.1 times within two years.

Canadian peer Rogers Communications , which scooped up rival Shaw Communications for C$26 billion in 2023, offers a cautionary tale. S&P Global Ratings expected debt to EBITDA to fall to 4 times by 2025 from 5.4 times immediately after closing. Analysts now expect Rogers to get there about three years late. Its shares have fallen by roughly a fifth.

Quebecor might have some tricks up its sleeve. Charles Nadim of Fiera Capital, an investor in both companies, points to non-core assets like Telus’ digital unit and its for-sale health business as quick potential divestitures. Add in some rural fiber networks, and selling these pieces could generate perhaps C$10 billion. If done within a year, that should reduce the total outlay by enough to lift returns closer to 8%, Breakingviews calculates. It’s still a thin margin and requires everything going right.

Furthermore, a hefty 60% premium to Telus’ November 13 share price loses some shine when set against the stock’s 28% fall year-to-date, prior to the announcement. This isn’t even to mention potential roadblocks put up by merger watchdogs at the Competition Bureau and Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission. Fiera thinks the deal would allow an enlarged company to compete against Elon Musk’s Starlink. The billionaire’s modifications of service in Ukraine and ambition to disrupt US wireless providers do make any alternative appealing. But how a legacy service provider in a market as small as Canada can boost a local champion against a practical monopolist is unclear. The more plausible outcome is a costly repeat of past telecom empire-building.

Follow Pranav Kiran on Bluesky and X.

CONTEXT NEWS

Canadian telecommunications firm Quebecor on November 16 said that it had sent rival Telus a proposal to acquire the company.

Under the proposal, Telus shareholders would receive C$6.35 in cash and 0.17 class B shares of Quebecor for each Telus share, for an implied value of C$19.45 per share. The proposal represents a 60% premium to Telus’ closing price on November 13.

Telus said on November 16 that the company’s board received an initial proposal on June 27, an amended proposal on November 9 and formed a special committee to review the offer. The committee has identified “significant regulatory and execution risks” associated with the proposed transaction.

TD Securities is advising Telus. Quebecor has hired JPMorgan as a financial adviser, Bloomberg reported on November 16 citing people familiar with the matter.

data.title: Astor Group subsidiary Oscilion to develop HPM demonstrator for FMV
data.description:
Scandinavian Astor Group AB (publ) (“Astor Group” or the “Company”) announces that its subsidiary Oscilion EW Systems AB (“Oscilion”) will carry out a three-year development project for the Swedish Defence Materiel Administration (FMV). The project aims to develop a demonstrator based on high-power microwave (HPM) technology to evaluate its potential for future weapon applications.

Oscilion has signed an agreement with FMV for a three-year development project funded by FMV, with co-funding from Oscilion. The agreement is of limited financial significance to Astor Group but represents an important step in the further development of Oscilion’s expertise in HPM technology. The project will commence in Q4 2026 and is scheduled for completion in Q2 2029.

“We are proud that FMV has selected Oscilion for this assignment. We have strong technical expertise in electronic warfare and look forward to working with FMV to apply this expertise in developing an HPM technology demonstrator,” says Fredrik Bergman, CEO of Oscilion EW Systems AB.

For Oscilion, the project represents a multi-year undertaking that builds on the company's expertise in electronic warfare. The demonstrator will be used to test and evaluate the technology.

“Oscilion combines proprietary products and systems with specialist expertise in electronic warfare. The project with FMV builds on this foundation and leverages the company's ability to translate technical expertise into practical solutions. We see this as an important recognition of Oscilion's capabilities,” comments Martin Elovsson, CEO of Astor Group.

data.title: 'Bluenami' green energy boost only reaches so far
data.description:
By Antony Currie

Fighting climate change just got easier in the United States. The Democratic Party’s sweeping successes in this month’s midterm elections ousted some key climate-sceptic Republican lawmakers. Voters also expressed their unease over the rapid growth of power- and water-hungry artificial intelligence data centres. Add the high price of fossil fuels brought about by President Donald Trump’s war on Iran and the prospects are improving for ramping up renewable energy and laying the groundwork for the US to rejoin international efforts to reduce global warming. Shares in American cleantech companies like GE Vernova , Brookfield Renewable Partners and Fluence Energy jumped 5% or more on the election results. But the green energy boost delivered by the so-called "bluenami" will only reach so far.

The electoral surge has registered in Antalya, the Turkish city where delegates have gathered for the COP31 climate summit. Combined with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's surprise re-election in Brazil last month, the US results boosted the mood at the United Nations confab where the host country, along with president of negotiations Australia, is pushing for an agreement to increase the proportion of global final energy demand coming from electricity to 35% by 2035, from 22% today. The upbeat atmosphere in the halls and country pavilions at the Expo Centre just a few kilometres outside the ancient Roman Mediterranean resort is in stark contrast to the brave faces attendees tried to put on two years ago in the Azerbaijani capital, Baku. That event took place a week after Trump retook the White House; his campaign included a promise, later carried out, to remove the United States from the Paris agreement for a second time.

There are good reasons to be optimistic. Voters in Texas, for example, not only elected climate-conscious Democrat Gina Hinojosa as governor, but also evicted the state's Republican attorney-general and comptroller. The pair had played key roles in the backlash against environmental investing that cowed financial institutions from BlackRock to Bank of America into playing down some of their climate policies - a process known as "greenhushing" - watering them down, or abandoning them entirely.

Big companies may now be more willing to openly discuss these principles again. The Lone Star State governed by Hinojosa is more likely to join neighbouring Democrat-controlled New Mexico and others in adopting more stringent rules on oil-and-gas pollution, which would reduce emissions of carbon dioxide and methane. Meanwhile, Congress under Democratic control is likely to reassert its role as a check on the executive branch's actions. The White House's suppression of renewable energy projects may be among past decisions lawmakers choose to investigate.

The case for rapid installment of cleantech looks straightforward on paper. The price of batteries and other kit is falling globally, performance is improving, and competition is increasing. Meanwhile, the cost of gas turbines has at least tripled while buyers face waits of up to eight years. As former US climate envoy John Kerry told the crowd in Antalya, it has “never been easier, cheaper or more exciting to do the right thing”. Besides, US firms have been doing it anyway: despite the Trump administration's fondness for coal, oil and gas, renewables accounted for more than 90% of the energy added to the system last year, according to the US Energy Information Administration. In the second quarter of 2026, companies placed orders for wind turbines equivalent to 2.8 gigawatts, the highest since the final three months of 2023, per Wood Mackenzie.

Much of that demand stems from the need to get projects up and running before tax credits introduced by Joe Biden's Inflation Reduction Act, and later eviscerated by Trump, come to an end. Those sweeteners are unlikely to return unless Trump makes an improbable policy U-turn or Democrats can persuade 11 Republican Senators to join them in overriding a presidential veto on any bill proposing their reinstatement.

The US is also missing out on some of the steep drop in global solar and battery costs. That's because the White House imposed tariffs of between 50% and 248% on clean tech from China, which is both the runaway leader in manufacturing photovoltaic modules and power cells and the biggest player in wind power. Democrats are just as wary as Republicans of the rising power of the People's Republic. However, politicians are also eager to reduce high energy prices; the tension between those competing considerations is likely to grow if Congress passes a bipartisan bill to speed up permitting for power and infrastructure projects.

There's also little prospect of an imminent American return to international climate diplomacy. Representatives of US states and cities have been on the ground in large numbers in Antalya, as at previous events. Gavin Newsom and Michelle Lujan Grisham, the outgoing governors of California and New Mexico, respectively, both made the trip. Trump, though, pulled the federal government out of not only the Paris agreement, but also the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, the overarching body on which the process is based. While it's not clear whether a president has the authority to unilaterally remove the country from an international treaty ratified by Congress, any future Democratic president hoping to rewind the clock would face a major - and time-consuming - legal battle.

Perhaps that's not as important as it used to be. While an engaged, positive US contribution to climate negotiations would be welcome, Washington exerts influence, both for good and ill, behind the scenes anyway. And the energy insecurity and higher fossil-fuel prices imposed on the world by the war on Iran have turned Trump into an accidental environmentalist: his actions have made solar, batteries and electric vehicles more economically appealing. That's especially true in countries from Australia to India to Pakistan, which have responded to the disruption in the Strait of Hormuz by speeding up their electrification push.

US companies are less likely to benefit, though. Trump's war on renewables has allowed China to consolidate its position as the dominant provider of clean tech. That may help explain why shares in Stateside companies from NextEra Energy to First Solar for the most part ceded their post-election gains. While the "bluenami" is good news for combating carbon emissions, its global reach is limited.

data.title: Activist Carronade raises Brookdale stake above 5%, pushes for changes
data.description:
Key points:
  • Carronade expected to file 13D disclosing stake above 5% and plans for changes, sources say
  • Fund may press Brookdale on capital allocation, M&A strategy and REIT conversion, sources say
  • Carronade held roughly 4% of Brookdale at end-September, regulatory filing shows

By Svea Herbst-Bayliss

Activist Carronade Capital has grown its stake in Brookdale Senior Living to more than 5% and wants the largest operator of senior housing in the US to boost its sagging share price, three people familiar with the matter said.

Over the last six months, Brookdale's stock price tumbled 35% amid lower occupancy rates, worries about this year's earnings and the specter of rising interest rates, analysts said.

For Carronade, an investor in Brentwood, Tennessee-headquartered Brookdale since 2024, the recent drop created an opportunity to both grow its stake and press for more forceful changes more quickly.

Those could include tactical and strategic options, ranging from how the company allocates its capital to how it views its mergers and acquisitions strategy, said the people, who were not permitted to discuss the hedge fund's plans publicly.

The six-year-old hedge fund, which invests $4.5 billion in assets and whose top executives previously worked at prominent activist firm Elliott Investment Management, owned a roughly 4% stake at the end of September, according to a regulatory filing.

Now the hedge fund is expected to make another filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission – a so-called 13D filing – detailing its current holdings of more than 5% and its general plans to push for changes, the people said.

Carronade is the most recent activist to engage with the company, which has a market capitalization of roughly $2 billion and has seen its share price drop 80% from its all-time high of $46.96 in 2006. It closed trading at $8.59 on Wednesday.

Last year a failed proxy fight by Ortelius Advisors and pressure from other investors likely accelerated the board's decision to install industry executive Nick Stengle as CEO in late 2025, analysts said.

With baby boomers moving into senior living communities at rising rates, investors and bankers see potential for the company to perform better. Analysts at Jefferies said in a recent report that Brookdale's real estate portfolio alone, comprising 32,367 units, is worth $24.50 a share.

Carronade has been in contact with management and is likely to step up its engagement to discuss possible portfolio optimization, better disclosure to investors and a possible transformation into a real estate investment trust, the people said.

A Brookdale representative did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

As M&A has boomed this year, the housing sector has attracted attention. Funds associated with merchant bank BDT & MSD Partners in October agreed to buy a majority stake in Sunrise Senior Living, and Sonida closed its $1.8 billion acquisition of CNL Healthcare Properties earlier this year.

Carronade was launched by Dan Groper, one of legendary hedge fund manager and Elliott founder Paul Singer's early analysts and later portfolio managers, during the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020. Health restrictions forced the team to cancel its roadshow and launch with $50 million, a large portion of which came from Groper's personal bank account. Andy Taylor, Carronade's head of research, also worked at Elliott.

data.title: Novartis drops after updating mid-term outlook
data.description:
Novartis shares fell in Zurich on Thursday after the Swiss drugmaker updated its mid-term guidance, indicating a 5% compound annual growth rate for net sales from 2026 to 2031 on a forex-adjusted basis.

The revised outlook fell short of the 5% - 6% forex-adjusted CAGR the company projected last year for 2025- 2030 and followed several trial setbacks the Basel, Switzerland-based company faced recently.

Shares of Novartis fell in September after a pair of Phase 3 trial failures for its RNA-based therapy del-desiran added through its $12B buyout of Avidity Bio in 2025 and a heart disease therapy it developed with Ionis Pharmaceuticals .

Novartis is already countering generic competition targeted at its heart drug Entresto, and its breast cancer therapy Kisqali and autoimmune disease therapy Cosentyx are also set to lose market exclusivity by 2031.

However, the company raised peak sales guidance for several key brands, including multiple sclerosis therapy Kesimpta and cholesterol drug Leqvio, which are now projected to generate $6B - $8B and $4B - $5B in peak sales, respectively. The company said it is on track to return to the previously targeted over 40% core operating income margin by 2029.

“As a pure-play innovative medicines company, Novartis has a strong track record of sales growth and core margin expansion, and in 2026 we expect to grow through the largest loss-of-exclusivity impact in our history,” added Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan.

data.title: Front-year prices gain on hydro scarcity, firmer gas prices
data.description:
Nordic front-year power prices rose on Thursday, as a widening hydro deficit, persistent dry weather forecasts and firmer European gas prices heightened concerns over supply in the hydropower-dependent region.

  • The Nordic front-year contract (NSBLYc1) gained €0.40, or 0.5%, to €77.10/MWh as of 1224 GMT

  • The Nordic front-quarter baseload power contract (NSBLQc1) edged down €0.26, or 0.2%, at €134 per megawatt hour (MWh)

  • "Hydro scarcity is the core driver. The most striking datapoint is regional. In one key southern Norwegian price area the stored water volume has not been this low in roughly thirty years," said Artem Bakushev, Head of Risk, Monaxa

  • Nordic water reserves available 15 days ahead (PCAEC00) were seen at 23.01 terawatt hours (TWh) below normal, the lowest level since July 17, compared with 22.23 TWh below normal on Wednesday

  • "High price levels in Central Europe are also reflected in Nordic and Finnish prices through transmission connections, especially during periods of low wind power generation," Bakushev added

  • European spot power prices rose on Thursday as wind power supply was forecast to fall and temperatures were expected to drop

  • "The weekend and next week will be largely dry and partially sunny with no significant precipitation," said LSEG meteorologist Georg Mueller

  • "The week after next week will likely be also mostly dry but potentially a bit milder with more near-normal temperature. Major wet and mild spells are not likely before December 5," Mueller added

  • Drier weather and low reservoir levels reduce hydropower availability, tightening the power market and supporting Nordic power prices in the hydropower-reliant region

  • Germany's year-ahead power contract (TRDEBYc1), Europe's benchmark, was up €2, or 1.4%, at €141 per MWh

  • In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract fell €0.11, or 0.1% to €81.67 a ton

($1 = 0.91 euros)
